title-proc.eng: Fire Remediation Works at Mill Court, Bandon, Co. Cork

description-proc.eng: The project involves the execution of fire remediation works to an existing 37-unit residential development located at Mill Court, Bandon, Co. The objective of the works is to address identified fire safety deficiencies in order to bring the building into compliance with current fire protection and life safety standards outlined in TGD Part B (Fire Safety) of the Building Regulations and other relevant codes such as IS 3218:2913 for fire alarm systems. The scope of the remediation works includes, but is not limited to: • Installation of fire-stopping systems at service penetrations and wall/floor junctions. • Replacement or upgrade of fire-rated doors, closers, and seals to comply with TGD-B. • Retrofitting of cavity barriers around gas flues and behind external cladding. • Façade treatments including removal and reinstatement of cladding for fire barrier installation. • Fire alarm cable rerouting and improvements to service risers and shafts. • Sealing of socket/switch boxes within fire-rated partitions. • General improvement of compartmentation and passive fire protection measures. All works will be undertaken within a live residential environment, requiring a high level of coordination to minimise disruption to residents.

title-proc.eng: 81322201 - Expert pool for advisory services on vehicle electrification in Latin America

description-proc.eng: Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) are at a critical moment in its transport decarbonization journey. The transport sector is one of the region"s largest and fastest-growing sources of greenhouse gas emissions, driven by entrenched car dependence, under-investment in public transit, high exposure to urban air pollution, and unequal access to mobility. While many countries have abundant low-carbon electricity sources (hydro, wind, solar) and growing political commitment to climate goals - for instance, zero emission targets for fleet acquisition and operation - the conditions for scaling e-mobility are not yet in place: pilots and early adopters are evident, but high capital costs, regulatory uncertainty, and infrastructure gaps continue to constrain large-scale deployment. Often the barriers to establishing these conditions are related to the following key challenges: regulatory, policy & institutional gaps; high upfront costs & financing barriers; technical know-how & operational capacity; infrastructure & grid readiness; and equity, gender & social inclusion. The E-Motion Program is commissioned by the Green Climate Fund (GCF) to the Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean (CAF) and the Agence Française de Développement (AFD) as accredited entities, executing entities, and co-financiers for the Financial Assistance (FA). GIZ takes part in the program as the executing entity for Technical Assistance (TA). The TA is integrated into the Mobilize Net Zero Project of the International Climate Initiative (IKI). In the program, GIZ implements large parts of the TA, while CAF and AFD are mainly implementing the FA. E-Motion represents one of the most comprehensive regional efforts to decarbonize the transport sector in LAC. It is anchored in two complementary parts: sub-program 1, implemented by GIZ and AFD in Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Mexico, and Peru; and sub-program 2, implemented by GIZ and CAF in Panama, Paraguay and Uruguay. Together, they constitute a multi-country platform supporting the transition toward low-carbon, inclusive, and resilient transport systems. They combine policy and institutional strengthening with investment in e-mobility infrastructure and fleets, creating the enabling conditions for large-scale transformation. The program addresses key challenges and structural barriers that hinder the large-scale deployment of e-mobility in fleets in LAC, with primary focus on buses and their supporting infrastructure but also dealing with fleets of light commercial vehicles (LCV). E-Motion"s objective is to translate climate ambition into practical transformation, building the institutional, financial, and technical foundations that enable countries to move from framework to fleet. Its TA and FA model strengthens governance, mobilizes investment, builds capacities, and delivers concrete e-mobility solutions on the ground. GIZ intends to contract a service provider to implement and support the TA activities of the program, while working in close contact with the GIZ team and program partners. Thus, the contractor will perform activities related to 5 core areas: - policy, governance and regulation for building coherent, inclusive, and harmonized policy frameworks - market development, finance and business models to enable financial viability and to mobilize investment - infrastructure, energy and technology for large-scale e-mobility deployment - fleet deployment and operations bringing e-mobility into practice through large-scale fleet deployment - capacity development, awareness and knowledge exchange building institutional, industry and human capacities

L’infrastructure comprend principalement des boîtes à gants ainsi que des équipements pour le traitement, la préparation et l’analyse des combustibles. Par ce démantèlement, l’exploitant de l’installation remplit les obligations du KEG et du KEV. L’objectif de l’appel d’offres est d’élaborer un concept pour le démantèlement de cette infrastructure, leur démontage et leur mise en service, ainsi que de réaliser les mesures de démantèlement.

Die Infrastruktur umfasst hauptsächlich Gloveboxen sowie Geräte zur Behandlung, Vorbereitung und Analyse von Brennstoffen. Durch deren Rückbau erfüllt der Anlagenbetreiber die Verpflichtungen nach KEG und KEV. Ziel der Ausschreibung ist es, ein Konzept für den Rückbau dieser Infrastruktur, deren Demontage und Inbetriebnahme zu erstellen sowie die Rückbaumassnahmen durchzuführen.
description-proc.eng: Within the scope of this tender, it is planned to dismantle the infrastructure of two alpha laboratories of the PSI hot laboratory (Hotlab), which was used for fuel research programs between 1979 and 2005 and is in a controlled area. title-proc.eng: Agreement for the execution of various topographical tasks

description-proc.eng: 5-year agreement for the execution of various topographical tasks involving the Fluxys' pipeline network. Fluxys constructs, manages and operates an infrastructure for high-pressure gas transmission by pipeline in Belgium. Actually, this network is about 4 200 km long. The technical and administrative data for this network are given in a database which is used by various departments in the company. This database — which is spatial — plays a key role in the operation of the pipeline network. This means that a lot of importance is attached to the accuracy of the data. The 3-dimensional aspect of the database is mainly the result of topographical surveys. Fluxys mainly uses external surveyors to conduct these surveys. The tasks involving new and/or existing Fluxys' pipelines and substations may include: (a) terrestrial site survey and mapping of new and/or changed topography; (b) terrestrial site survey and mapping of new and/or changed topography vis-à-vis the existing topography; (c) terrestrial site survey and mapping of a new site profile; (d) terrestrial pipeline survey + accessories and mapping of a new pipeline profile; (e) digital output — supplying files in all of the following formats: Microsoft Excel format, Microstation DGN format and the Fluxys' exchange format XSUF. As well as to take note of a ETL-application (Extract,Transform en Load) such as FME (Feature Manipulation Engine); (f) the use of other surveying techniques alongside topographical surveying, e.g. active radio detection and ground tracing; (g) tasks involving the preparation for site levelling; (h) the tasks involving the purchase and sale of Fluxys sites include the preparation of survey and/or demarcation reports.

title-proc.eng: 81322153-Leadership for Health system strengthening

description-proc.eng: The GIZ Global Program (GP) BACKUP Health, in alignment with the mission of the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (GFATM), seeks to address critical issues in health system strengthening through a specialized leadership program. This tender calls for a contractor to lead the coordination, adaptive design, management, and implementation of a tailored leadership program (L4HSS) inspired by the Leadership for Universal Health Coverage (L4UHC) flagship program of the P4H Network. Launched in 2013 by GIZ and the World Bank, L4UHC aims to empower key decision-makers in partner countries. The primary goal of this consulting project is to support GP BACKUP Health partner countries in their health system reform processes. The focus will be on coalition building, enhancing leadership competencies, and establishing joint action initiatives that result in concrete policy options for integrating Health Technology Management (HTM) services into national systems, ensuring financial sustainability. The detailed objectives are to: 1. Strengthen Leadership Competencies: Provide leaders of health finance reforms the opportunity to enhance their leadership and sectoral competencies at an executive level. 2. Develop Collective Vision: Aid leaders in developing a collective vision and commitment to achieving tangible results. 3. Foster Collaboration: Promote collaboration among key cross-sectoral stakeholders. 4. Establish Collective Action Initiatives (CAIs): Contribute to the creation of implementable national CAIs aimed at achieving GP BACKUP indicators. Specifically, this involves producing nine design options for ATM integration that, through coaching, will result in at least six strategic, legislative, or planning documents by the project's end. 5. Provide Tools and Techniques: Offer tools and techniques for mapping complex systems, analyzing stakeholder influence, and addressing collective action problems. 6. Peer-to-Peer Exchange: Facilitate peer-to-peer exchange among leaders and provide inputs from technical experts towards national objectives. 7. Co-Create Innovative Solutions: Enable leaders to co-create and implement innovative solutions to health system strengthening challenges through CAIs. 8. Coaching Support: Provide coaching support to leaders as they address these challenges. 9. Demonstrate Results: Organize and coach health system strengthening leaders around a time-bound commitment to demonstrate results. The contractor will be responsible for the end-to-end implementation of the leadership program, ensuring adaptive design and effective coordination. The program will leverage the established L4UHC framework to provide a comprehensive and tailored experience for participants. The contractor will facilitate workshops, coaching sessions, and peer exchanges, ensuring that leaders are equipped with the skills and tools necessary to drive health system reforms. At the conclusion of the project, the following outcomes are anticipated: - Enhanced leadership competencies among health finance reform leaders. - A collective vision and commitment towards achieving concrete results. - Established collaboration among cross-sectoral stakeholders. - Creation of nine design options for ATM integration, leading to six strategic, legislative, or planning documents. - Improved tools and techniques for addressing complex system challenges. - Successful peer-to-peer exchanges and technical expert inputs. - Co-created innovative solutions to health system strengthening challenges. - Demonstrated results through time-bound commitments. - Scaled good practices through peer learning and diverse country experiences.

The project is subject to strict environmental controls in accordance with the plans, particulars and conditions associated with the project consents. Environmental management will form a key part of the successful execution of this project. In particular, it is a requirement that construction is carried out in accordance with the Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP), other environmental management plans required under the EIAR and NIS, relevant Wildlife and derogation licenses to create and manage a suitable receiving environment for the Kerry Slug in the area affected by the proposed greenway. The work will support seabird tracking activities and will contribute to a transboundary seabird conservation strategy and action plans for priority threatened seabird species. BTO is a project partner in the ACCLIMATISE project, supported by PEACEPLUS, a programme managed by the Special EU Programmes Body (SEUPB). ACCLIMATISE is led by the Agri-Food and Biosciences Institute (AFBI). Within this project, BTO is leading Work Package 2: ‘Transboundary Conservation Strategies and Sustainable Management of Marine Predators’. As part of this work, BTO (co-leading with the RSPB) will carry out extensive seabird tracking and ecological studies across Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland. This specifically includes tracking to investigate the at-sea distribution, foraging ecology, and flight height in breeding Black-legged Kittiwake Rissa tridactyla (hereafter Kittiwake), Northern Fulmar Fulmarus glacialis (hereafter Fulmar), Common Guillemot Uria aalge (hereafter Guillemot), and Razorbill Alca torda. This tender relates specifically to the supply of seabird tracking and biologging tags to support this work. The appointment of a Tenderer will be by a process of open tender. The requirement is set out in the Specification herein. General information on the British Trust for Ornithology is also available at www.bto.org

title-proc.eng: Master mix for one stage real time reverse transcription PCR (RT-qPCR) at Helse Bergen HF and Helse Førde HF

description-proc.eng: The aim of the procurement is to enter into regional parallel framework agreements for the procurement of master mix for one stage real time reverse transcription PCR (RT-qPCR) for the microbiological department at Helse Bergen HF and Helse Førde HF. The Microbiological Department at Helse Bergen HF and Helse Førde HF would like tenders for PCR mastermix for detecting microbial RNA from patient samples (real time reverse transcription PCR/RT-qPCR). The mastermix shall mainly be used for detecting RNA viruses in airway samples and the estimated sample volume at Helse Bergen HF is 350,000 – 450,000 PCR reactions per annum. Helse Førde Health Trust estimates that the sample volume is 60,000 - 70,000 PCR reactions per annum. A high quality mastermix is required that provides high sensitivity, high specificity and stable results over time. The mastermix must be optimised for multiplexing and not very sensitive to any PCR inhibitory substances in the eluat. Helse Bergen uses Roche ́s Flow platform to analyse the airway analyses, which consist of Hamilton robots and Light Cycler 480/LightCycler Pro. By Helse Førde, LightCycler480II and Rotorgene RGQ are used. Ready pipetting PCR boards may be queued up and waiting for the free PCR instrument. The reagents must therefore endure standing for some time at light/room temperature after pipetting. See Annex 2 - Requirement Specifications tab 3. Minimum requirements and 4. Quality, as well as Annex 2a - Testing Form for further details. An initial testing will be carried out at Helse Bergen HF of mastermix candidates with the department ́s primers/probes for relevant genes on the Flow system. Mastermixer that do not deliver an equivalent or better result than the current reagents (c.f. minimum requirements nos. 7 and 8) will not be considered further. The mastermix candidates who deliver satisfactory results will proceed to an expanded trial at both Helse Bergen HF and Helse Førde HF, if they are based on the set award criteria have the possibility to go victorious out of the tender.

title-proc.eng: Procurement of winter maintenance services for Statnett in the Southern operations area

description-proc.eng: Statnett SF, Southern Operations Area, hereinafter referred to as the Client or Statnett, currently operates a number of substations with associated access roads spread across Agder and Rogaland. To ensure proper operation and safety during the winter season, Statnett needs to enter into framework agreements for various winter maintenance services for this area. The work mainly includes snow plowing, handling of snow masses, procurement and storage of grit material, sanding when required, handling of snow poles, weather monitoring, and emergency preparedness. Statnett has varying needs for assistance at the different locations covered by the agreement. The need varies, among other things, based on how critical it is that each individual substation is accessible at all times, and whether Statnett has its own resources to carry out winter maintenance at the substations. See Appendix 1 for an overview of the substations. For three substations, there is a requirement that the supplier has full responsibility for carrying out winter maintenance, and these substations must be accessible in terms of passability at all times. This therefore requires both high preparedness and continuous weather monitoring. These substations are geographically located in both Agder and Rogaland. For five substations, snow plowing services will be ordered as needed. These substations do not have the same requirement for constant accessibility, but the supplier must have sufficient capacity to carry out winter maintenance within a reasonable time, in accordance with the deadlines set out in Appendix 1. The substation at Stølaheia is under construction and is expected to be completed within two years. In addition, Statnett’s own employees are responsible for emergency preparedness and for carrying out winter maintenance at a further five substations. For these substations, assistance will be requested as needed, for example in the event of insufficient internal capacity. Furthermore, another license holder is responsible for winter maintenance at eight substations. Statnett wishes to have the option to request assistance with winter maintenance tasks at these locations from the framework agreement supplier(s) as well. The contract supplier has no obligation to provide winter maintenance services at these substations, and therefore no preparedness or additional capacity in terms of personnel and machinery is required for these locations. It is reserved that the needs of individual substations may change during the contract period. A framework agreement will be entered into with one supplier. The commencement date is 15 October 2026

title-proc.fin: Procurement of accessibility monitoring tool - TRAFICOM/163741/02.03.01/2024
title-proc.eng: Procurement of accessibility monitoring tool

description-proc.fin: The Finnish Transport and Communications Agency Traficom invites Service Providers to participate to a Procurement of accessibility monitoring tool. Traficom monitors the accessibility of approximately 240 websites annually with an automated tool. Accessibility requirements are defined in the Act on the Provision of Digital Services. Traficom currently uses the SALVIA system developed for this purpose, which is based on the open source QUALWEB testing core. When the contract period ends at the end of 2026, we will tender a solution for a tool for checking the accessibility of websites with an automated tool for monitoring the work. Traficom acquires Software service for simplified monitoring of website accessibility as a SaaS solution. The Software service is used to automatically check whether a website contain content that does not meet the accessibility requirements of the Act. Accessibility requirements are defined in the European harmonized standard EN 301549 Accessibility requirements for information and communication technology products and services. The objective of the procurement is to facilitate the implementation of the Subscriber's accessibility checks and to free up resources for actual monitoring work instead of developing and maintaining the current monitoring system. With the procurement, the Subscriber will have access to new features for monitoring work and new reporting methods that will improve the service received by the monitoring targets. We aim for four important strategic benefits: • Reliability: The system meets the need of the supervisory authority to monitor websites in accordance with the obligations set, and the testing rules are updated when standards or other obligations are updated. • Efficiency: the Supplier is responsible for maintenance and updates, which frees up staff work for monitoring • Quality: modern features and reporting methods improve the service to the monitored objects and reduce the workload of the Subscriber • Security: servers in the EU, the system is tailored to Subscriber's needs. The subject of the procurement is a Software service for monitoring the accessibility of websites as a SaaS solution, accessible via a browser-based user interface. This simplified monitoring procedure, the selection of targets and their number are described in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/1524 in point 1.3 of Annex I (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32018D1524#anx_I ). Traficom acquires a Software service that enables its staff to perform automated accessibility inspections in accordance with the simplified monitoring method. The Subscriber performs monitoring evaluations throughout the year. Accessibility monitoring is aimed at websites that can be freely browsed or behind a login. Traficom defines the monitored targets and sites annually, either at one time or in several batches. Traficom selects some of the pages or the entire site to be evaluated. Evaluations are performed to complete web pages in the website. Each of the web pages selected for evaluation are identified by a unique URL or by other means e.g. in cases where the website is a single-page app or otherwise contains dynamic content that cannot been reached with a URL alone without additional events performed by the user or automated scripts. Traficom shall submit to the Website Service Provider an inspection report on the performance of the inspection and its results, which shall include, among other things, the accessibility deficiencies found on the evaluated pages. If necessary, Traficom shall provide guidance to the service provider subject to supervision on correcting the deficiencies. Traficom currently supervises approximately 240 websites annually. It is possible that the number may increase to, for example, 500 websites due to regulatory changes. However, Traficom does not commit to the number of websites to be supervised. Websites selected for supervision will generally undergo one inspection during one supervision period. The number of pages to be inspected on a website may vary, but maximum number of pages per website is 150. The website may be selected for inspection again in the next supervision period, and therefore the previous assessments with reports must be available in the system. Traficom also performs in-depth review of websites. This in-depth review procedure, the selection of targets and their number are described in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/1524 in point 1.2 of Annex I (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32018D1524#anx_I) At the moment in-depth review is done manually by inspectors. If the new Software service provides in-depth review, Traficom may implement the feature during the implementation project. The whole Software service and all Traficom's material processed in the software service must be located in the European Union or the European Economic Area (EEA).

Evaluations are performed to complete web pages in the website. Each of the web pages selected for evaluation are identified by a unique URL or by other means e.g. in cases where the website is a single-page app or otherwise contains dynamic content that cannot been reached with a URL alone without additional events performed by the user or automated scripts. Traficom shall submit to the Website Service Provider an inspection report on the performance of the inspection and its results, which shall include, among other things, the accessibility deficiencies found on the evaluated pages. If necessary, Traficom shall provide guidance to the service provider subject to supervision on correcting the deficiencies. Traficom currently supervises approximately 240 websites annually. It is possible that the number may increase to, for example, 500 websites due to regulatory changes. However, Traficom does not commit to the number of websites to be supervised. Websites selected for supervision will generally undergo one inspection during one supervision period. The number of pages to be inspected on a website may vary, but maximum number of pages per website is 150. The website may be selected for inspection again in the next supervision period, and therefore the previous assessments with reports must be available in the system. Traficom also performs in-depth review of websites. This in-depth review procedure, the selection of targets and their number are described in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/1524 in point 1.2 of Annex I (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32018D1524#anx_I) At the moment in-depth review is done manually by inspectors. If the new Software service provides in-depth review, Traficom may implement the feature during the implementation project. The whole Software service and all Traficom's material processed in the software service must be located in the European Union or the European Economic Area (EEA).
